Raised in a Catholic environment, he grew up valuing compassion and justice, particularly influenced by the discrimination faced by his Jewish friends. During World War II, Beltrami studied medicine while secretly aiding the French Resistance. From 1942, he served as a courier and provided medical assistance to those in need. After the war, he dedicated himself to improving healthcare access in underserved communities, establishing clinics in rural areas of southern France. He passed away on November 12, 1991, leaving behind a legacy of kindness and courage.
